errors.text_span: The left chart, "AttentionInfluence," shows a total of 14 major categories
errors.evidence: The left chart has 6 inner main categories, not 14. The 14 visible items are a mix of inner and outer slices.

errors.text_span: The right chart, "FineWeb-Edu Classifier," displays 11 major categories
errors.evidence: The right chart has 6 inner main categories, not 11. The listed 11 items again mix inner and outer slices.
There is no slice labeled "Tech & Society" in either chart. The corresponding brown inner slice on the left is "Tech & Engineering" (12), not "Tech & Society" (8).

The left chart's brown inner category is labeled "Tech & Engineering 12"; the machine text shortens it to "Engineer" but keeps the value 12. This is only a label mismatch if treated as a separate mapping error; however the number itself is correct.
The categories "Manage" and "Policy" are not dark red. In the figure, they are blue on the left chart and blue for Manage on the right; Policy does not appear on the right chart.
Education is shown in green/mint in the figure, not teal; although similar, the color assignment is not exact in the description.
Health & Medicine is rendered in light blue in both charts, not the generic blue claimed here.

Diseases is a blue outer slice, but the description assigns it inconsistently with other blue/light-blue categories and mislabels the color mapping across the chart; however the figure does show a blue Diseases segment, so this is not an error.
Animal & Plant is pink/red in the figure, not dark red.
Manage is blue in the left chart and blue in the right chart, not dark red.
Policy is blue in the left chart and does not appear in the right chart; it is not dark red.
Fin & Law is a cyan/blue inner slice on the left, so this is broadly correct; however the text also incorrectly includes it in the global color list without noting it appears only on the left.
Teaching & resources is green/mint in the figure, not teal.
This category does not exist in the figure. The machine-generated description invents a slice/label not present in either chart.

The description identifies the charts and some categories, but it does not clearly state the chart purpose as the reference does (distribution of categories for AttentionInfluence and FineWeb-Edu Classifier).
The description fails to mention that the chart labels are placed inside the slices and that there is no legend, both of which are visible and noted in the reference.

errors.text_span: The charts do not include a legend or percentage labels inside the slices, but the numbers shown represent the count or weight of each category.
errors.evidence: The figure is a pie/sunburst chart with no axes; the statement about percentage labels is correct in the negative sense, but the phrase implies a legend/measurement interpretation that is not relevant. More importantly, the numbers are percentages in the reference context, not generic counts or weights.

errors.text_span: the largest categories (Education, Teaching & resources, and Science & technology education in the right chart) placed prominently at the top.
errors.evidence: This is an interpretation rather than a measured value, but it is misleading: the right chart does show Education largest, yet the ordering/top prominence is not a quantitative claim supported in the description and the exact notion of 'descending size order' is not consistently verifiable from the figure.
